guides.title: Start Here
guides.summary: First-day priorities, campaign controls, starter teams, and what to buy in the Black Market.

sections.title: Start with the Normal campaign
items: Push the Normal campaign as far as your team can go. Normal clears raise offline earnings. Come back for three-star rewards, Hard, [[t:黑潮]], and Commander-only clears when you need their rewards.

When you stall, try controlling the Commander manually to interrupt the boss. Clear another stretch of tower stages, level the team, and try the campaign again. Clearing Normal Chapter 14 opens Misty Mountains, where deeper clears raise offline earnings again.

screenshots.title: Campaign screen and Idle Reward Chest
screenshots.alt: Campaign battle with the Idle Reward Chest open. Red boxes mark the stage banner, retreat, Fatigue, reward rates, Quick Idle, deployed Blackguards, and battle controls.
notes: The top banner shows Arklance on Normal difficulty, Chapter 1, stage 9, substage 4. The retreat button beside it resets the stage when used during a boss fight.

Fatigue (FP) refills at the daily reset and can also be restored with items. Kills and chests use FP automatically when they drop loot. At zero FP, they grant no equipment or items. The EXP meter to the right tracks bonus experience from kills and resets daily.

The row beneath the meters shows offline reward rates. Some gear and items drop while you’re offline, so you can close the game. Tick the box beside Claim to send loot to your Bag automatically when the chest fills up.
Each Quick Idle costs 50 FP and gives 3 hours of Echoes and 1 hour of Mana Crystals. At zero FP it gives no rewards. The author recommends using the daily Quick Idle attempts while you’re leveling.
On the right, Boss starts boss fights automatically, Auto makes the Commander move automatically, and Skill lets deployed Blackguards cast on their own. Turn on 2× and 3× together for 6× speed.
The portraits at the bottom show your deployed Blackguards. Tap the chest between them to open this panel. The City button returns you to town, and the Bag is available inside a stage.

sections.title: Check the one-time gear picks
items: Chapter 1-6-4 offers [[g:聚能之铠]]. The wiki recommends it as a versatile early armor pick.
Check [[g:战狂]] at 2-21-4, [[g:邪徒]] at 3-3-4, and [[g:妖精秘手]] at 3-6-4. The wiki lists other ways to obtain these pieces, with a resource cost.
The wiki flags [[g:夺魂之戒]] at 4-8-4 and [[g:蔷薇之心]] at 4-13-4. It lists a skin purchase as the alternative source if you miss the campaign reward.

sections.title: Build an inexpensive starter team
items: Put your best damage dealer on the field and use easier-to-awaken S-rank Blackguards to build support-slot bonuses. The wiki suggests building up an S-rank [[f:狩魔]] support first, adding [[f:前锋]] support, and considering [[c:神之嫡子]] and [[c:灵刃之主]] as later SS-rank options.
Before summoning, check the selected banner’s wish and pity rules. The beginner article describes carryover within a recurring banner of the same name. Individual banners can have their own rules.

sections.title: Level the Ancient Tree
items: Before level 400, the lowest-level Blackguard in your main slots sets the Tree’s cap. Upgrade and awaken easier-to-rank cards in those slots, then put rarer cards in linked slots so they can use the Tree’s recorded level.

From level 400 onward, invest directly in the Ancient Tree. Level skills before investing in specialization, which the wiki describes as a base-stat upgrade. For talents, start with the stat the Blackguard’s skills scale on, then choose offense or survivability by role.
The hidden-reward article shows a small Diamond pickup in a screenshot. Use the linked source to find its location.

sections.title: What to buy in the Black Market
items: The General Shop refresh button uses Ancient Coins from daily activity rewards. The first refresh costs 400. The author recommends stopping when the price rises.
The Academy Cup earns up to 600 Academy Coins per hour in the guide. Clear out the Rune Edge Reroll Stones before buying equipment.
Event shop stock changes with the event. The Sakura Shop screenshot below shows one rotation and the author’s priorities for it.

For the Great Temple, the author saves 430 Blacktide Medals for the Bounty Guide (90), Echo Resonator (110), Ancient Tyrant skin (30), and Mana Crystal Sensor (200). Using the Corridor Navigator (110) instead of the skin costs 510 in total and delays the Sensor.

screenshots.title: Black Market tabs and refresh button
screenshots.alt: Black Market with the General Shop selected. The tabs on the left and refresh button at the top have red outlines and yellow notes.
notes: The circular arrow at the top refreshes the General Shop. This is the main source of Locking Stones and Smoked Meat Chops.
The Corridor and Glory shops are the main places to buy SS Blackguard fragments.
The author usually skips the Guild and Misty shops and puts Guild Coins toward skill upgrades and Misty Coins toward relic upgrades.
In the Academy Shop, always buy the Rune Edge Reroll Stones and buy equipment if you urgently need it.

The Event Shop has limited-time stock. If you’re unsure what to buy, the author suggests checking with experienced players. Save up for Great Temple purchases because Blacktide Medals have few sources.

screenshots.title: General Shop purchases
screenshots.alt: Page 2 of the General Shop, highlighting Locking Stones, Smoked Meat Chops, discounted Restoration Stones, and the page arrows.
notes: Buy out the Locking Stones (锁定石) and Smoked Meat Chops (熏制肉排), boxed together in the top row.
Buy discounted items, such as the boxed Restoration Stones, when you need them.
Use the arrows at the bottom to check both pages. On page 1, buy Addition Stones, Removal Stones, Attribute Stones, Socket Drills, and Sweep Tickets as needed.

screenshots.title: Corridor Shop
screenshots.alt: Corridor Shop page with a grid of SS Blackguard fragments and an annotation across the top.
notes: Buy fragments for the SS Blackguard you need. Combine 90 matching fragments for one copy.

screenshots.title: Glory Shop
screenshots.alt: Glory Shop page with SS Blackguard fragments and an annotation across the top.
notes: Exchange for fragments of the SS Blackguard you need. Combine 90 matching fragments for one copy.

screenshots.title: Misty Shop gear, page 1
screenshots.alt: Misty Shop page 1 with the Ancient Arcanist’s Barrier boxed in the bottom row.
notes: If you want to skip farming [[g:死灵法盾]], you can buy [[g:古老魔盾]] as a substitute, though the author advises against it. Skip the other items on this page.

screenshots.title: Misty Shop PvP gear, page 2
screenshots.alt: Misty Shop page 2 with the Dragonkin boots and Dragonbane shield boxed in the top row.
notes: The boxed Dragonkin Stride boots (龙裔步伐) and [[g:龙猎大盾]] are PvP gear. Exchange for them only when you need them. Skip the other items on this page.

screenshots.title: Time Shop Black Stones and gear
screenshots.alt: The Time Shop tab beside Misty Shop. Boxes mark the Raging Beast Black Stone, Mirage Stones, and a column of headgear.
notes: Use the tabs above the items to switch between Misty Shop and Time Shop.
Buy the high-grade Raging Beast Black Stone when you can, unless you’re building a team without Physical damage dealers.
Consider Mirage Stones (幻境之石) later. If you can’t farm the headgear you need, prioritize the boxed headpieces. Buy the other gear according to your build.

screenshots.title: Academy Shop equipment
screenshots.alt: Academy Shop page 1. Red boxes mark the belt and two pieces recommended for Soul of Divinity.
notes: Buy the Rune Edge Reroll Stones first. After that, consider one [[g:王室荣尊]] as a stopgap. For [[c:神之嫡子]], the author suggests at most one copy each of [[g:蛇灵之怒]] and the Soulblood Ring (魂血源戒) if you need them.

screenshots.title: Academy Shop Rune Edge Reroll Stones
screenshots.alt: Academy Shop page 4, with the sold-out Rune Edge Reroll Stone boxed on the bottom row.
notes: Buy out the Rune Edge Reroll Stones (符文洗边石). The author stresses that they’re scarce in the mid- and late game.

screenshots.title: Event Shop and Sakura exchanges
screenshots.alt: Sakura Shop II under the Event Shop. The annotated boxes mark the event tabs, currency, rune chest, and first- and second-priority exchanges.
notes: The author describes the Sakura Shop opening near the start and middle of each month, with a separate tab for limited-time events. Spend FP to earn the Sakura currency shown at the top right.
Early on, you can exchange for up to two Precision Cast Rune Chests (精铸符文宝箱). The author usually skips them later.
First priority is the Lunar Cleansing Stone (月辉洗涤石), boxed in red. The cyan boxes show the second priority, which includes Advanced Adjustment, Adjustment, Addition, and Removal Stones.

screenshots.title: Great Temple Defense Strength and first exchanges
screenshots.alt: Great Temple page 1 with the Defense Strength bar, Pureblood Crystals, Bounty Guide, Echo Resonator, and Corridor Navigator highlighted.
notes: Defense Strength is shown at the top and determines what you can buy. At level 1, buy the Bounty Guide (悬赏指引仪). It unlocks level 2, when you can buy the Echo Resonator (回响共鸣器). Save the Corridor Navigator (回廊路向仪) for later so it doesn’t slow early progression.

After the Bounty Guide, Echo Resonator, and a cheap skin take you to level 3, you can raise Defense Strength quickly by buying Pureblood Crystals (纯血晶石) one at a time. Make each purchase separately and stop at level 5.

screenshots.title: Great Temple Mana Crystal Sensor
screenshots.alt: Great Temple page 2 with the Mana Crystal Sensor boxed in the top-left corner and the page arrows marked.
notes: Go to page 2 and prioritize the Mana Crystal Sensor (魔晶感应器) as soon as Defense Strength reaches level 3. It increases Mana Crystal earnings while idling.

screenshots.title: Great Temple Ancient Tyrant skin
screenshots.alt: Great Temple page 6 with the Ancient Tyrant skin boxed in the bottom row.
notes: After the Bounty Guide and Echo Resonator, the Ancient Tyrant skin (古代暴君) on page 6 is the cheapest way to reach Defense Strength level 3 and unlock the Mana Crystal Sensor.

guides.title: Gear to Lock
guides.summary: Search the wiki’s decomposition keep list by English name, Chinese name, or slot.

sections.title: Before bulk decomposition
items: Lock the listed items in your inventory before running bulk decomposition. The wiki flags them for unique effects, such as [[t:物理强度]], [[t:法术强度]], [[t:全伤害类型减免]], [[t:技能冷却]], and [[t:吸血]], that can stay useful beyond the item’s level.

Keep uncertain Misty Mountains clear drops until you’ve checked their effects. The three-star flag marks items the wiki recommends fusing. Open the gear entry to see the effect and who uses it when that information is available.

guides.title: Monthly Resources
guides.summary: What to save for event milestones and what to buy in the Black Market.

sections.title: Save resources for the events that use them
items: Crafting and synthesis events reward spending materials in batches. Set aside affix-stone fragments and equipment-leveling materials until you can check which actions count for the upcoming event.
For the Blackguard leaderboard event (黑卫之巅), compare ticket prices and milestone rewards before buying entries. Pick a milestone target if you’re playing for rewards.

Heart of Summon rewards Blackguard summons. If your team can already progress, save summon currency and calculate how many pulls you need from the current event screen. Budget [[t:圣血晶石]] separately for banners that require them.
For FP-spending events such as Blaze the Trail and The Sakura Season, check the overlap before using stored FP. One action may contribute to more than one event.

sections.title: Black Market and redeem codes
items: The wiki prioritizes lock materials and the food item 熏制肉排 in the Black Market. Check the next refresh price before refreshing again.
Use the wiki’s homepage to look up listed codes and their restrictions. Confirm expiry and server or platform eligibility in your client or the official announcement.

guides.title: Gear Upgrades
guides.summary: Forge, fuse, enhance, and transfer gear without spending scarce materials too early.

sections.title: Forge and fuse
items: A blueprint unlocks a forging recipe. Forging earns experience toward blueprint choices. The wiki says one blueprint can contribute up to 200 experience and that lineup [[t:幸运]] affects the quality roll.

Pick a base worth keeping before using rare modification materials. For gear whose effect improves with fusion, the wiki suggests fusing same-name, same-quality feeder copies into a level-capped base. The feeder copies do not need to share the base’s level cap.
Plan your target prefixes and suffixes before rerolling. Save scarce [[t:神话]]-tier materials for pieces you expect to keep, and check the affix ranges and exclusions shown in the modification screen.

sections.title: Transfer enhancement, transfer affixes, or inherit
items: Enhancement transfer moves the donor enhancement level to the target and resets the donor’s enhancement. Affix transfer replaces the target affixes and empties the donor’s affixes. The wiki lists [[t:史诗]] as the minimum quality for affix transfer.

Inheritance consumes the donor. The wiki’s eligibility checklist calls for an inscribed donor capped at level 700 or higher, a target with an equal or higher cap, and matching slot and affix groups. Preview what will carry over before confirming.

sections.title: Enhance Black Stones
items: Eligible Black Stones come from deeper Misty Mountains floors. The wiki recommends starting with +3 on several good stones, then committing more shards to exceptional rolls. Its examples pair [[t:魔力]] with [[t:法术强度]] or [[t:力量]] with [[t:物理强度]], and prioritize [[t:体质]] for tanks.
Enhancement raises a random eligible stat. Check the stone’s quality, existing stats, and the cost of the next upgrade before spending shards.

sections.title: Misty Mountains
items: Once Normal Chapter 14 is clear, push Misty Mountains while your team can beat the floor timer. The wiki distinguishes a kill that earns the clear from a kill fast enough to unlock the next floor. Use the in-game timer to judge whether to retreat or finish.
The time-space variant (时空幻境) unlocks after floor 750 according to the wiki. It has a separate entry allowance and exchange currency. Check the encounter modifiers before committing the team.

Deep Mist requires completing the third Forgotten Realm area and reaching 50% exploration there. Use Commander skills on elite enemies and let your Blackguards handle regular enemies. The earlier bands have random Black Stone drops. The table below shows the targeted bands after floor 850.

sections.title: Forgotten Realm
items: Prepare three teams and give them enough durability for consecutive fights. Rear spawns can reach your back line, and the last fight of the first area copies your lineup.

In the second and third areas, control effects help break the boss’s shield. The wiki recommends [[c:纯净史莱姆]] as a budget option for shield breaking. Build your teams to survive the shield phase before chasing more damage.

sections.title: Journey Stories and Black Abyss
items: The four Journey Story walkthroughs below cover separate encounters and drop pools. Choose a story based on the gear you need, then check its unlock requirements.
In Black Abyss, the boss’s element can vary after entry. The wiki gives example lineups for Frost, Lightning, Fire, and Physical teams. Prepare more than one element and keep the ticket cost in mind.

guides.title: Teams & PvP
guides.summary: Awakening, support slots, Front stars, and how to read the arena rankings.

sections.title: Awaken your Blackguards
items: S and SS Blackguards use same-class cards and duplicates to awaken, raising their level caps. SP Blackguards progress through awakening qualities with their level. The wiki lists [[t:永恒]] as an important milestone for damage reduction and later rune slots.

sections.title: Plan the Fronts before spending stars
items: Both deployed and support-slot Blackguards contribute Fronts. The wiki suggests stacking a basic [[f:狩魔]] bonus early and adding [[f:前锋]] or [[f:秘术]] as your roster grows.
Extra Fronts normally need matching picks on at least two Blackguards. Use the wiki simulator to check the thresholds before investing, and use the English Fronts reference to look up the effects.

sections.title: Read PvP rankings by role
items: Decide what the team needs first: opening control, protection and recovery, or burst damage. The PvP source calls out effects such as opening silence, Rage denial, team control immunity, and healing denial.

Check whether a ranking assumes late-game gear, blood ranks, or a specific partner. The English PvE rankings answer a different team-building question. See the dated PvP source below for the roster ranking.

guides.title: Combat & Gear by Effect
guides.summary: Scaling, damage types, status effects, and situational gear lookups.

sections.title: Read the skill’s scaling and damage type
items: The stat a skill scales from and the damage type it deals are separate fields. A skill can scale from [[t:法术强度]] and deal physical damage. Use its scaling to choose the base stat and its damage type to choose the appropriate damage bonus.

The wiki describes [[t:法术伤害增幅]] as applying to Fire, Frost, and Lightning. Basic attack effects and other skills can use different accuracy and crit checks. Check the skill text when choosing between attack crit and [[t:技能暴击]].

sections.title: Look up effects by the problem you’re solving
items: Use [[t:初始怒气]] to bring the first ultimate forward, [[t:怒气恢复]] to support later ultimates, or [[t:技能冷却]] when the skill timer is the bottleneck. Use the linked wiki lists to find gear, then check its English effect in the item catalog.

[[t:冰缓]] reduces attack speed and Rage recovery. [[t:点燃]] applies fire damage over time. [[t:感电]] makes a target take more Lightning damage as stacks accumulate. Numbers depend on the item or skill applying the effect.
Chinese guides often shorten stats and roles. For example, 物强 and 法强 mean [[t:物理强度]] and [[t:法术强度]]. 主C means the main damage dealer, and CD refers to cooldown.

guides.title: Additional Systems
guides.summary: Collection rewards, beasts, enchantments, treasures, and guild upgrades.

sections.title: Soul items, beasts, and enchantments
items: The wiki lists a collection reward (魂器) at 75% SS collection progress. Claim it in the collection interface and check the effect before equipping it to an SP Blackguard.
The beast table (幻兽) groups options by basic-attack element, scaling stat, and whether they have an active skill. Compare active utility and cooldown alongside damage.
The enchantment reference (附魔) lists point thresholds and level-by-level effects. Pick an effect relevant to the team, then check how many points you need to activate it.

sections.title: Treasures and guild progression
items: Look up treasures (宝物) by acquisition area, eligible Front, and kill requirements. Some effects improve farming or drops, while others add combat stats.

For guild progression (公会跃升), the wiki lists the Gold dungeon, eligible codes, and trading as sources of Gold. Compare the next upgrade’s cost with its practical effect and check whether older team guides assume any guild upgrade levels.
